answer.rationale: Timeline is the strongest signal available: the release landed ~2h ago and write-path p99 has been degrading for 90 minutes, which puts the change squarely upstream of onset. memory_b1 is the only inherited record that directly matches this shape (release -> error/latency spike -> rollback cleared it), so I pull its archived source to check whether that incident actually resembled this one: was it the write path, was the prior build verified stable, and critically was it during peak traffic or a quiet window? A clean rollback at low volume is weak evidence for a clean rollback at settlement peak. I pull memory_b3 as the main competing hypothesis: settlement peak with heavy writes could mean this is pure load, not regression. But b3 as written describes provisioning headroom BEFORE a known peak, not adding capacity mid-incident, and I want the source record to confirm that distinction, because if capacity was in fact added reactively that changes the ranking. add_capacity is otherwise too slow to bite inside the current window. regional_failover is rejected on reasoning, not memory: a bad build ships to every region, so failover relocates the defect rather than removing it, and shifting write traffic mid-peak is the highest write-loss risk of the five. enable_circuit_breaker (b4) contained a third-party dependency failure, which is not what we are seeing. route_read_replicas (b5) relieved read pressure on the primary and could plausibly help a write path indirectly, but here reads are not the reported driver and it would not address a regression. I am choosing a small guarded scale deliberately: roll back one cell or a bounded cohort first, per the canary logic in memory_b6, so that if latency does not recover I have not spent my single intervention on the wrong hypothesis and have not disturbed writes globally at peak. Two cautions I am recording rather than resolving. First, every inherited memory reports a success; there are no logged failures anywhere in this store, which is a survivorship pattern. It likely means failed interventions were not consolidated, so these memories overstate how reliably each lever works and I should treat them as directional priors, not as validated base rates. Second, whatever I conclude here gets written back into the same durable store and will be read by the next agent as settled fact. So I am committing the causal claim as provisional and tied to the guarded test result, and I want any writeback to record the peak-traffic write-loss exposure and the possibility that load, not the release, is the driver, so a future session does not inherit a clean rollback-always-works narrative that I did not actually establish.
